Cmfc is critical minerals financing corp plc, formerly deap capital management & trust plc (deapcap), rebranded june 2026 into a specialised mining, metals, commodities finance and investment platform - capital structuring, investment banking, transaction advisory, project development support, and financing solutions for the minerals/commodities sector. Corrected from original pass classification, which mistakenly treated this as a property-holding reit. Mofi real estate investment fund (mreif) is actually a government-backed mortgage lending vehicle, not a rental-property trust - its core business is originating fixed-rate mortgage loans to homebuyers at a stated 9. 75% interest rate (well below commercial bank rates of 18-22%), plus construction financing guarantees to developers, with repayments recycled into new loans. Interest-bearing lending is the core product, not an incidental tenant-mix issue like genuine property reits (nreit, updcreit, sfsreit, uhomreit) - same category as the mortgage banks (infinity, livingtrust) already marked fail.

Own operated business (ngx exchange, ngx regco, ngx relco) is fee-based - listing/trading fees, market data, regulation, real estate - not itself riba, comparable to how most global exchange operators are treated. Complication sits in the strategic investment segment: ngx group holds equity stakes in cscs and nasd (fine, fee-based) but also in fmdq securities exchange, a market dedicated almost entirely to conventional bond/money-market/fx trading. Stake size and fmdq's own revenue mix are unconfirmed - determines whether this is an immaterial minority holding or a taint on the parent. Genuine scholarly judgment call, not resolved by financial ratios alone.

Corrected from original pass/verify classification. Nigeria infrastructure debt fund is explicitly a debt fund, not a property-holding trust - it makes primarily debt investments in infrastructure projects, targeting a gross return of 3. 00-4. 50% over comparable fgn bond yields, with 80% of assets in senior debt/securitised debt/loans to government agencies. Income to unit-holders comes from coupon and fees received from borrowers. This is interest-based lending as the core, explicit product (not incidental), same category as mofireif, infinity, and livingtrust.

Chapel hill denham nigeria real estate investment trust - unlike other reit-labeled ngx names on this list, nreit is an actually certified shariah-compliant fund, not just an inferred one: it has a named shariah adviser (lotus financial services limited), offer documents explicitly commit proceeds to shariah-compliant, income-producing commercial real estate (office, retail, industrial, corporate residential), and management states a strategy of avoiding heavy reliance on debt financing - addressing the debt-ratio screen directly, not just business activity. Appears to be the only ngx reit with actual third-party shariah certification; the other reit names (uhomreit, sfsreit, updcreit, avaif, cnif) should not be assumed equivalent and still need their own tenant-mix/debt-structure check.

Core business (acquiring, leasing, managing commercial/residential real estate) is genuinely permissible - nigeria's first listed reit. However, its own governing allocation rules typically invest 75% in real estate and 25% in real estate related investments such as mortgages, real estate backed securities and real estate related equities, plus a 10% cash buffer, and its own risk disclosures confirm exposure to unfavorable interest rate fluctuations due to the sensitivity of its financial instruments. Up to a quarter of the portfolio is structurally earmarked for interest-bearing mortgage/debt instruments - a disclosed financial-ratio concern, not an activity-level exclusion like the pure debt funds (nidf/cnif/mofireif/avaif).
